hints: Start by drawing out methylpropene clearly, it is 2-methylpropene, $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$.
Remember that every single bond is one sigma, while one C=C double bond is one sigma plus one pi.
Count all the C-H and C-C sigma bonds separately, then add the one sigma from the double bond to get the total.
walkthrough:
**Draw the structure first**

Methylpropene is 2-methylpropene with formula $C_4H_8$. Its displayed structure is $CH_2=C(CH_3)_2$.

That is one $C=C$ double bond, two $C-C$ single bonds, and eight $C-H$ single bonds.

**Count the pi bonds**

Only multiple bonds contain pi bonds. A double bond is made of one sigma plus one pi.

$$ \text{1 } C=C \text{ double bond = 1 } \sigma + 1 \pi $$
So total $\pi = 1$.

**Count the sigma bonds**

Every single bond is one sigma, and the double bond also contributes one sigma.

$$ \sigma = 8 \text{ (C-H)} + 2 \text{ (C-C)} + 1 \text{ (from C=C)} = 11 $$
So we have 11 sigma and 1 pi, which matches one of the rows.

options.A: Not correct. 1 pi is right, but 10 sigma is one too few. This happens if you forget to count one of the C-C or C-H sigma bonds. There are 8 C-H plus 3 C-C sigma frameworks, giving 11 in total.
options.B: Not correct. Both counts are wrong. 10 sigma undercounts by one, and 2 pi is a common trap of thinking a double bond has two pi bonds. A double bond is 1 sigma + 1 pi only.
options.C: Correct and well done. The molecule $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$ has 8 C-H sigma bonds, 2 C-C sigma bonds, and 1 sigma from the C=C, giving 11 sigma total. The one C=C gives just 1 pi bond.
options.D: Not correct. 11 sigma is right, but 2 pi is wrong. Students sometimes confuse a double bond with a triple bond. A triple bond would have 2 pi bonds, but an alkene C=C has only 1 pi bond.
